mainTopic: The power of בית דין versus a husband's cancellation, and whether גילוי דעתא cancels a גט
overview: The גמרא answers a challenge against רב נחמן. He let a husband cancel a גט even though this seems to weaken בית דין, yet in the case of orphans dividing an estate he argued 'otherwise, what power does בית דין have?' The answer is that money matters are different from matters of איסור. Next comes the story of גידול בר רעילאי. His wife put off receiving her גט, and he happily said 'ברוך הטוב והמטיב'. אביי and רבא disagree whether this cancelled the גט, and the root of their argument is גילוי דעתא: does clearly showing you don't want the גט count as cancelling it? Each side brings proofs from real cases: רב ששת, רב יהודה's witnesses with gourds in their ears, and the man stopped by the ferry. Each proof is pushed away. Two more stories about marriage deadlines are shown to depend on the same argument, since אין אונס בגיטין. The amud ends with two rulings like רב נחמן.

steps.title: רב נחמן seems to contradict himself about the court's power
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about orphans dividing an estate, and רב נחמן's own ruling that grown orphans cannot protest because that would weaken בית דין. This clashes with his ruling about cancelling a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that when orphans come to divide their father's property, בית דין appoints a guardian and picks a fair share for each one. When they grow up, they can protest. But רב נחמן himself said that when they grow up they cannot protest, because otherwise, what power would בית דין have?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge against רב נחמן. It shows that in the orphans case he himself used the argument 'otherwise, what power does בית דין have?'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, רב נחמן ruled that a גט cancelled by the husband really is cancelled. He ruled this way even though רבן שמעון בן גמליאל objected that this weakens בית דין. But here רב נחמן himself relies on that same 'power of בית דין' argument to keep a court's decision standing. So how can he ignore that argument when it comes to a גט?

keyTerms.meaning: A guardian or steward appointed to manage property for someone
To protest or object, here meaning to demand a new division
What power does the court have? An argument that the court's decisions must be upheld
His own, meaning a statement by רב נחמן himself

steps.confusionAlert: The first part, which says they CAN protest, is the ברייתא. רב נחמן disagrees with it and says they CANNOT. Do not mix up the two.

phrases.english: Orphans who came to divide their father's property,
the court appoints a guardian for them,
and they choose a fine portion for them.
When they have grown up, they can protest.
And Rav Nachman himself said:
When they have grown up, they cannot protest;

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִם כֵּן, מָה כֹּחַ בֵּית דִּין יָפֶה?
phrases.english: for if so, what power does the court have?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge against רב נחמן's ruling about cancelling a גט, which began just before this passage.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that a husband's cancellation of a גט works
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן himself relies on 'what power does בית דין have' in the orphans case. So he should also accept that argument against cancelling a גט.

steps.title: Money matters are different from prohibition matters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the orphans case is about money, while the גט case is about איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is a money matter; here it is a matter of prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction in just four words. In money matters, the court's power wins. In matters of איסור, it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With money, בית דין can decide who owns what, so protecting its authority is worth an imperfect division. With a גט, the question is whether a woman is still a married woman. We cannot let her remarry just to protect the court's honor if the husband really cancelled the גט. So רב נחמן is consistent.

keyTerms.meaning: There, the case brought as a challenge
Here, the case we are discussing
Matters of prohibition, such as marriage and divorce

steps.whatToRemember: The argument 'what power does בית דין have' carries weight in money matters. It does not override a question of איסור, such as whether a woman is truly divorced.
steps.whyThisMatters: The split between ממונא and איסורא is a common way the גמרא settles contradictions all across ש״ס.

phrases.english: There it is a money matter,
here it is a matter of prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between the two cases: money versus prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן's reasoning about the court's power should apply to every area of law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The court's power wins only in money matters. In matters of איסור like a גט, the husband's cancellation still works.

steps.title: גידול בר רעילאי's wife puts off her גט
steps.stepSummary: גידול בר רעילאי sent a גט to his wife. She asked the agent to come back tomorrow. When the husband heard this, he said 'ברוך הטוב והמטיב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: גידול בר רעילאי sent a גט to his wife. The agent went and found her sitting and weaving. He said to her, 'Here is your גט.' She said to him, 'Go away for now, and come back tomorrow.' He went back to the husband and told him. The husband began by saying, 'Blessed is He Who is good and does good.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up the next step. There, אביי and רבא will argue about what the husband's words did to the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband was clearly happy that the גט had not yet been delivered. The question is whether showing that happiness counts as cancelling the גט. If it does, the agent can no longer deliver it.

keyTerms.meaning: The agent, the messenger carrying the גט
Blessed is He Who is good and does good, a blessing over good news

phrases.english: Giddul bar Re'ilai
sent a bill of divorce to his wife;
the agent went,
found her sitting and weaving,
he said to her: Here is your bill of divorce.
She said to him: At least go away now,
and come tomorrow.
He went to him and told him.
phrases.notes: The agent went back to the husband and told him what had happened.

phrases.english: He opened and said:
"Blessed is He Who is good and does good."

steps.triggerLanguage: גִּידּוּל בַּר רְעִילַאי שַׁדַּר לַהּ גִּיטָּא לִדְבֵיתְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a real case about whether words of happiness cancel a גט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband who heard his גט was not yet delivered said 'ברוך הטוב והמטיב', which raises the question of whether the גט is cancelled.

steps.title: אביי and רבא disagree whether the גט was cancelled
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the husband was only expressing happiness, so the גט is not cancelled. רבא says his blessing cancels the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says: He said 'Blessed is He Who is good and does good,' and the גט is not cancelled. רבא says: He said 'Blessed is He Who is good and does good,' and the גט is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי and רבא disagree about the result of the story. Did the husband's blessing cancel the גט?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the husband was glad. אביי holds that being glad is just a feeling and is not an act of cancelling. רבא holds that such clear joy shows the husband no longer wants the גט delivered, and that is enough to cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: The גט is cancelled and can no longer be used

steps.confusionAlert: Both אביי and רבא quote the exact same words of the husband. Their only difference is the ending: 'ולא בטל גיטא' (not cancelled) versus 'ובטל גיטא' (cancelled).
steps.whatToRemember: אביי says joy at a delay does not cancel a גט. רבא says it does.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
"Blessed is He Who is good and does good,"
and the bill of divorce is not cancelled.
Rava said:
"Blessed is He Who is good and does good,"
and the bill of divorce is cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: בָּרוּךְ הַטּוֹב וְהַמֵּטִיב, וְלָא בָּטֵל גִּיטָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the legal result of the story in step 3, with two opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: the blessing does not cancel the גט. רבא: the blessing cancels the גט.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what basic principle אביי and רבא are arguing about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the deeper issue is behind the argument of אביי and רבא about the husband's 'ברוך הטוב והמטיב'. This is a setup question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we only know the two rulings. The גמרא now wants the general principle underneath them, so that the argument is not just about one story.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the underlying principle behind the two rulings in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The general principle behind the argument of אביי and רבא.

steps.title: They argue about showing intent regarding a גט
steps.stepSummary: The argument is about גילוי דעתא. אביי says showing intent does not cancel a גט, and רבא says it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about showing one's intent regarding a גט. אביי holds that showing intent regarding a גט is not significant. רבא holds that showing intent regarding a גט is significant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the argument is about גילוי דעתא: what happens when the husband clearly shows he doesn't want the גט, but never actually says 'I cancel it.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's 'ברוך הטוב והמטיב' showed he was glad the גט was delayed, but he never said the words of cancelling. For אביי, only real cancelling counts, so the גט still works. For רבא, clearly showing your wish is enough, so the גט is cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: showing what you want through words or actions, without a formal declaration
it is nothing (it does not count)

steps.whyThisMatters: This turns one story into a general rule about cancelling a גט, which the rest of the סוגיא tests with proofs.

phrases.english: They disagree about showing one's intent regarding a bill of divorce
phrases.notes: Showing intent means the husband makes clear he doesn't want the גט, but never actually says 'I cancel it.'

phrases.english: For אביי holds:

phrases.aramaic: גִּלּוּי דַעְתָּא בְּגִיטָּא לָאו מִלְּתָא הִיא,
phrases.english: Showing intent regarding a bill of divorce is not significant,
and רבא holds:
Showing intent regarding a bill of divorce is significant.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument is whether גילוי דעתא is enough to cancel a גט: אביי says no, רבא says yes.

steps.title: רבא's proof from the story with רב ששת
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a story: a man forced to give a גט told the witnesses 'רב ששת says to cancel the גט,' and רב ששת required a new גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From where do I say this? רב ששת forced a certain man to give a גט against his will. The man said to the witnesses: 'This is what רב ששת told you: cancel the גט.' And רב ששת required him to give another גט.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a story to prove that showing intent is enough to cancel a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man didn't say 'I cancel.' He only put the words in רב ששת's mouth, which showed he didn't want the גט. Even so, רב ששת treated the גט as cancelled and made him write a new one. So רבא says showing intent counts.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do I say it? (a proof is coming)
he took from him, forced out of him

phrases.english: רבא said: From where do I say this?
For רב ששת forced out a bill of divorce
phrases.notes: He means רב ששת pressured the man into agreeing to have a גט written.

phrases.english: from a certain man against his will,
and he said to the witnesses:
phrases.notes: The one speaking here is the husband, not רב ששת.

phrases.english: This is what רב ששת said to you:
to cancel the bill of divorce.
And רב ששת required him to give another bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא supports his side of the argument defined in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that גילוי דעתא cancels a גט.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב ששת, who required a new גט after the husband said 'רב ששת says to cancel.'

steps.title: אביי rejects רבא's proof
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the husband himself really cancelled the גט. He only blamed רב ששת out of fear of being beaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי? Would רב ששת cancel other people's גיטין?! The husband himself cancelled it. And the reason he told them this was because of the lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes away רבא's proof by reading the story differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת would never cancel a man's גט for him, so the words 'cancel the גט' must have been a real cancellation by the husband himself. That is a real cancellation, not just showing intent. He put it in רב ששת's name only so the בית דין's men wouldn't beat him for going against רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say...? (a challenge that rejects an idea)

phrases.english: And אביי (how would he answer)?

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מְבַטֵּל גִּיטָּא דְּאִינָשֵׁי הֲוָה?!
phrases.english: Is that to say רב ששת would cancel other people's bills of divorce?!
He (the husband) cancelled it himself;
and the reason he said this to them,
was because of the lashes.
phrases.notes: He was afraid the בית דין's men would beat him for going against רב ששת. The extra letter in square brackets is the corrected spelling.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַבָּיֵי – אַטּוּ רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מְבַטֵּל גִּיטָּא דְּאִינָשֵׁי הֲוָה
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only. רבא's view itself is not disproven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The story was a real cancellation by the husband, not mere showing of intent, so it proves nothing about גילוי דעתא.

steps.title: אביי's proof from the story with רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה forced a man to give a גט three times. The third time, he told the witnesses to plug their ears and write. They saw the man running after them, and still the גט worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: From where do I say this? רב יהודה forced the son-in-law of רבי ירמיה ביראה to give a גט, and he cancelled it. Again he forced him, and he cancelled it. Then again he forced him against his will, and told the witnesses: 'Put gourds in your ears and write it for him.' Now if showing intent regarding a גט were significant, they could see him running after them!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings his own story to prove that showing intent does not cancel a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses plugged their ears, so they could not hear any real cancellation. But they could still see the husband chasing them, which clearly showed he didn't want the גט. רב יהודה still let the גט go through, so showing intent alone does not cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: again, a second time (here it does not mean 'taught')
and if it would enter your mind (if you were to think)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the third time was a real cancellation. The witnesses couldn't hear anything, so all that was left was his running after them, which is only showing intent.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי: showing intent does not cancel a גט (proof: the running husband in the story of רב יהודה). רבא: showing intent does cancel a גט (proof: the story of רב ששת, which אביי pushes away).

phrases.english: And אביי said: From where do I say this?
For רב יהודה forced out a bill of divorce
from the son-in-law of רבי ירמיה ביראה,
and he cancelled it;
again he forced it out, and he cancelled it;
phrases.notes: Here תנא means 'again, a second time,' not 'a תנא taught.'

phrases.english: then once again he forced it out against his will,
and he (רב יהודה) said to the witnesses:
Put gourds in your ears and write it for him.
And if it would enter your mind
that showing intent regarding a bill of divorce is significant,

phrases.aramaic: הָא חָזוּ לֵיהּ דְּקָא רָהֵיט בָּתְרַיְיהוּ!
phrases.english: but they see him running after them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבא's proof, אביי brings his own proof.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that גילוי דעתא does not cancel a גט.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב יהודה, whose גט worked even though the witnesses saw the husband running after them.

steps.title: רבא: The Husband Was Running to Say 'Hurry Up'
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that in רב יהודה's case, the running husband may have wanted the witnesses to hurry, not to stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא? He would say that the man running after them may have wanted to tell them: 'Hurry, give her the גט quickly, so my pain can be over.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the proof from step 9. He says the husband's running does not clearly show that he wanted to cancel the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, a גט is only cancelled when the husband's intent is clear. Running after the witnesses is unclear: it could even mean 'finish this fast so my suffering ends.' Since nobody heard what he wanted, there was no real גילוי דעתא, so the גט stayed good.

phrases.english: And רבא? [How would he explain this?]
This, that he was running after them,
was in order to say to them:
Hurry, give it to her quickly,
so that the pain will be over
of 'that man.'
phrases.notes: 'That man' is a polite way of saying 'me.' He is talking about his own pain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 9 against רבא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רב יהודה's case does not work against רבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Running after the witnesses does not clearly show he wanted to cancel. It could mean he wanted them to hurry.

steps.title: אביי's Proof from the Man Stopped by the Ferry
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings שמואל's ruling: a man who reached the river on time but could not cross is not considered to have 'come,' so the גט takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: How do I know my view? A man told them, 'If I don't come within thirty days, this is a גט.' He came, but the ferry kept him from crossing. He shouted, 'See that I came! See that I came!' And שמואל said: that does not count as coming.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings his own proof that showing intent does not cancel a גט. He uses a case where שמואל ruled the גט works even though the husband clearly showed he did not want it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband made it clear that he wanted to be counted as having arrived, and that he did not want the divorce. Still, שמואל said the גט takes effect because he did not actually arrive. אביי reads this as: clear intent alone does not stop a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? (introducing a proof)

phrases.english: And אביי said:
From where do I say this?
For there was a certain man who said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא אָתֵינָא עַד תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין,
phrases.english: If I do not come within thirty days,
let it be a גט.
He came, but the ferry cut him off;
He said to them:
'See that I came, see that I came!'
And שמואל said:
That is not called coming.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא pushes back on step 9, אביי brings a fresh proof for his own side.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's view that גילוי דעתא does not cancel a גט.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's ruling on the man held back by the ferry: the גט took effect despite his clear protest.

steps.title: רבא: The Ferry Man Wasn't Cancelling, He Just Missed His Condition
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the ferry case is about failing to meet a condition, not about cancelling a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא? Was that man trying to cancel the גט? He was trying to fulfill his condition, and his condition was not fulfilled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects אביי's proof. He says the ferry case is a different kind of case altogether.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גילוי דעתא is about a husband trying to cancel the גט. The ferry man was not cancelling anything. He was trying to meet his condition ('I will come'), and he simply did not arrive. Since the condition failed, the גט works, and this tells us nothing about intent cancelling a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (introduces a pushback)

steps.whatToRemember: Cancelling a גט and failing to meet a condition are two different things. רבא says intent can cancel a גט, but intent cannot make a condition count as fulfilled when it really wasn't.

phrases.english: And רבא? [How would he answer this?]
Is that to say that there he wanted to cancel the גט?!
There he wanted to fulfill his condition,
and his condition was not fulfilled.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא – אַטּוּ הָתָם לְבַטּוֹלֵי גִּיטָּא בָּעֵי
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The ferry case does not prove anything about גילוי דעתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the ferry case the husband was not trying to cancel the גט. He was trying to meet a condition and failed, so the case is about a failed condition.

steps.title: The Man Who Promised to Marry Within Thirty Days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new story: a man said that if he did not marry within thirty days the גט would take effect, and at the deadline he said 'I tried.'
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who said to them: 'If I do not marry her within thirty days, let this be a גט.' When thirty days came, he said to them: 'Look, I made the effort.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the facts of a new case. This is setup: the ruling and the discussion come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the ferry case, this is a conditional גט with a thirty-day deadline. The new twist is that the husband claims he tried to fulfill the condition. The question waiting to be answered is whether trying is enough to stop the גט.

keyTerms.meaning: I made the effort, I took the trouble

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אִי לָא נָסֵיבְנָא עַד תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין –
phrases.english: If I do not marry her within thirty days,
let it be a גט.
When the thirty days arrived,
he said to them: Look, I made the effort.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲמַר לְהוּ: אִי לָא נָסֵיבְנָא עַד תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new case that is similar to the ferry case (a conditional גט with a thirty-day deadline) and sets up the next discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Facts only so far: a conditional גט with a thirty-day marriage deadline, where the husband claims he tried. Step 14 analyzes the case.

steps.title: Analyzing the thirty-day marriage case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what could possibly make the גט fail. It gives two possible worries. The 'I tried but couldn't' worry is rejected because אין אונס בגיטין. The 'he showed he doesn't want it' worry depends on the argument between אביי and רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What should we be worried about here? If it is because he was stopped by things beyond his control, there is no such excuse in גיטין. If it is because he showed that he doesn't want the גט, that is the argument between אביי and רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now decides the story from step 13, where the husband said 'I tried' at the deadline. It checks two possible reasons to doubt the גט and deals with each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'I tried' could be an excuse of אונס, but in גיטין a condition that was not met still counts as not met, even if he was stopped by something he couldn't control. It could also be a sign that he really doesn't want the גט (גלויי דעתא). Whether such a sign undoes a גט is exactly what אביי and רבא argue about, so this case depends on their argument.

keyTerms.meaning: What should we be worried about with it?
Being forced or stopped by things beyond your control
In a גט condition, 'I was stopped' is not an excuse
Showing, by words or actions, what you really want

steps.confusionAlert: 'אין אונס בגיטין' does not mean nobody is ever forced. It means a condition in a גט is still counted as broken even if the husband was stopped by something he couldn't control.

phrases.english: What should we be worried about with it?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the גט from the thirty-day story, where the husband said 'I tried.'

phrases.english: If it is because of something beyond his control,
there is no excuse of being stopped when it comes to gittin.
If it is because he showed what he wants about the get,
that is the argument of Abaye and Rava.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי נֵיחוּשׁ לַהּ? אִי מִשּׁוּם אוּנְסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the thirty-day case told in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What reason could there be to doubt this גט?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אונס is not a reason, because אין אונס בגיטין. גלויי דעתא depends on the argument between אביי and רבא.

steps.title: The אדר versus ניסן story
steps.stepSummary: A man set a deadline of ראש חודש אדר to marry, or else the גט would take effect. When אדר came, he claimed he had really said ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who said to witnesses: if I do not marry by ראש חודש אדר, let this be a גט. When ראש חודש אדר came, he said to them: I said ראש חודש ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new, similar story. This sets up the analysis in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the husband does not claim he was stopped. Instead, at the deadline he says the deadline was actually a month later. That raises the same question: does his statement make the גט fail?

keyTerms.meaning: I marry (I take her in marriage)
The start of the month, ראש חודש
The month of ניסן, the month after אדר

phrases.english: There was a certain man who said to them:
If I do not marry
by Rosh Chodesh Adar,
let it be a get.
When Rosh Chodesh Adar arrived,
he said to them:
I said by Rosh Chodesh Nisan.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲמַר לְהוּ: אִי לָא נָסֵיבְנָא לְרֵישׁ יַרְחָא דַּאֲדָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story parallel to the thirty-day case of steps 13 and 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case setup: a husband claims at the deadline that the deadline was really later.

steps.title: Same analysis for the אדר case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא runs the same two-part check. אונס is no excuse in גיטין, and גלויי דעתא depends on the argument between אביי and רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What should we be worried about? If it is because of something beyond his control, there is no such excuse in גיטין. If it is because he showed what he wants, that is the argument between אביי and רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats, almost word for word, the same analysis it gave for the thirty-day case. It applies it to the אדר story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though his claim is different ('I said ניסן' instead of 'I tried'), the possible worries are the same. Being stopped doesn't help a גט condition. His claim might show he doesn't want the גט, and that is the אביי–רבא argument. (Elsewhere the גמרא rules like אביי in this argument.)

keyTerms.meaning: Being forced; the Hebrew form of אוּנְסָא

phrases.english: What should we be worried about with it?
If it is because of something beyond his control,
there is no excuse of being stopped when it comes to gittin.
If it is because he showed what he wants,
that is the argument of Abaye and Rava.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאי נֵיחוּשׁ לַהּ? אִי מִשּׁוּם אוֹנֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same reasoning from step 14 to the new case in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What reason could there be to doubt the גט in the אדר case?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not אונס, because אין אונס בגיטין. גלויי דעתא depends on the argument between אביי and רבא.
steps.whatToRemember: In both stories the husband's last-minute words don't help him by claiming אונס. The only possible way they matter is as גלויי דעתא, which is the argument between אביי and רבא.

steps.title: First ruling like רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה follows רב נחמן, about cancelling a גט in front of two people.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows רב נחמן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives final rulings on the earlier parts of this סוגיא. This first one goes back to רב נחמן's view that a husband can cancel a גט in front of two people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the סוגיא there was an argument about how many people must be present for a husband to cancel a גט he sent. This line settles it: we follow רב נחמן, and two people are enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancelling a גט in front of two people

phrases.english: And the halacha follows Nachman;
phrases.notes: This means רב נחמן. It goes back to his view, earlier in the סוגיא, that a גט can be cancelled in front of two people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories and returns to an earlier argument in the sugya to give the final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A husband can cancel a גט in front of two people, like רב נחמן.

steps.title: Second ruling like רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again rules like רב נחמן, this time on his statement that the הלכה follows רבי in both of his disputes with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows רב נחמן.
steps.whatsHappening: The same words are repeated, but they give a second, separate ruling. It is about a different statement of רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן had said that the הלכה follows רבי in both places where he argues with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in this topic. This line confirms that we accept that ruling too.
steps.confusionAlert: The two lines are word-for-word the same, but they are not a copying mistake. Each one confirms a different ruling of רב נחמן.
steps.whatToRemember: The סוגיא ends with two rulings like רב נחמן. A גט can be cancelled in front of two people, and the הלכה follows רבי in both of his disputes with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

phrases.english: And the halacha follows Nachman;
phrases.notes: Same words, different ruling. This one confirms רב נחמן's view that we follow רבי in both of his disputes with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate final ruling following the first one.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי in both of his disputes with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, as רב נחמן ruled.
